clue.text: Butterfly down stalk

parts.note: to down a drink is to swallow it
to stalk someone is to tail them

explanation.surface: A butterfly flutters down onto a plant stalk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'down' and 'stalk' look like nouns in a nature scene but both are verbs here.
explanation.definitionFit: The swallowtail is a large butterfly named for the tail-like projections on its hind wings.

clue.text: Piano preferably features for sound mixer?

indicators.note: the outer word features (contains) the letter, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: 'I'd sooner' means I'd preferably, so sooner stands for preferably
P is the musical abbreviation for piano, meaning softly

explanation.surface: A query about a piano being the preferred feature for a sound engineer's mixing desk.
explanation.walkthrough: P goes inside SOONER. William Spooner was the Oxford don famous for swapping the starting sounds of words, hence a 'sound mixer'.
explanation.definitionFit: Spooner gave his name to spoonerisms, in which initial sounds of words get jumbled; the question mark flags the playful description.

clue.text: Unfamiliar, a claim on property

parts.note: a lien is a legal right to hold property until a debt is paid

explanation.surface: A strange legal claim on someone's property.
explanation.definitionFit: Alien as an adjective means strange or foreign, not known to one.

clue.text: Labour lass raised snail

indicators.note: in a down clue raised means the letters are read upwards, i.e. backwards

parts.note: a drag is a tiresome, laborious effort, so labour gives drag
gal is an informal word for a lass or girl

explanation.surface: A Labour Party woman has bred or lifted a snail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Labour' looks like the political party but is a toil word; 'raised' reverses DRAGGAL from bottom to top.
explanation.definitionFit: A snail is figuratively a slow person, just as a laggard is someone who falls behind.

clue.text: Attractive habit of champions

definitions.meaning: ... as an adjective means charming, appealing
champions are in the habit of ... matches

explanation.surface: Being attractive is a habit of champions.
explanation.definitionFit: A winning smile is an attractive one, and champions routinely keep on winning.

clue.text: Laud radical, a politician, praising more than is deserved

indicators.note: radical suggests drastic change, so the letters of laud are rearranged

parts.note: a Tory is a member of Britain's Conservative Party

explanation.surface: Praise a radical and a politician, flattering them beyond their merits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Laud' and 'praising' share a sense, but 'Laud' is only fodder here; 'radical' is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Adulatory describes excessive, fawning admiration, flattery beyond what someone has earned.

clue.text: Note, one is in church free from clerical doctrines

parts.note: la is the sixth note of the sol-fa scale
I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: in means the word is is placed within the church letters

parts.note: CE stands for the Church of England

explanation.surface: A note says one person in church is free of clerical teaching.
explanation.definitionFit: To laicise is to secularise, removing something from clerical control and putting it in lay hands.

clue.text: Call on farm before group arrival

indicators.note: before puts the farmyard call ahead of the group in the answer

parts.note: moo is the call of a cow on a farm
a ring is a group or gang of people

explanation.surface: A farmyard cry heralds the arrival of a group.
explanation.definitionFit: A boat mooring is its berthing on reaching port, so the word can stand for coming in to land.

clue.text: Crime in gang of men?

parts.note: male describes men
a faction is a group or gang within a larger body

explanation.surface: A question whether a crime was committed in a gang of men.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads 'gang of men' in reverse order: MALE comes first in the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Malefaction is a formal word for wrongdoing or a criminal act.

clue.text: Bad back prodded by our hospital nurse

indicators.note: being prodded means having something poked into it, so our goes inside
back says the word is read in reverse

parts.note: sin is wrongdoing, something bad
H is the standard map abbreviation for hospital

explanation.surface: A nurse with a bad back gets prodded at the hospital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' reverses the bad word to NIS before 'prodded by' opens it up; 'nurse' at the end is the verb, not a person.
explanation.definitionFit: To nurse something, such as a hope or a child, is to nourish or feed and foster it.

clue.text: With garden gone to seed, he's saved pineapple

indicators.note: he has saved means the letters he hold the rest within them

parts.note: taken as written
and means with, together with

indicators.note: a garden gone to seed is run down and disordered, so its letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A gardener whose plot has run wild has kept a pineapple plant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'With' is a synonym, not a link word, and ''s saved' reads as 'he has saved', a container. 'Pineapple' looks like fruit, but it was WWII soldiers' slang.
explanation.definitionFit: Pineapple was soldiers' slang for a hand grenade, from its segmented casing.

clue.text: Red, cardinal colour's third from the right

indicators.note: reading from the right means the letters run backwards

parts.note: nine is a cardinal number

indicators.note: third picks out the third letter of the word colour

explanation.surface: A cardinal's red robe is the third colour from the right.
explanation.walkthrough: NINE plus L (third letter of colour) gives NINEL, which 'from the right' turns round.
explanation.definitionFit: Lenin led the Russian Bolsheviks, and a Red is a communist.

clue.text: Yours truly is inspired by people after a film

indicators.note: after places the people construction behind a in the answer
inspired means breathed in, so the people word takes the other letters inside it

parts.note: a nation is a people
yours truly means me, the speaker, so 'yours truly is' is I'm

explanation.surface: The speaker is inspired by people after seeing a film.
explanation.definitionFit: An animation is a cartoon film made from drawn or computer-generated frames.

clue.text: Fresh — as hospital linen may be?

definitions.meaning: cheeky or overfamiliar, as fresh does
linen destined for a hospital ward

explanation.surface: Clean sheets ready to go out to the hospital.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading splits the answer as FOR WARD.
explanation.definitionFit: Fresh in the sense of impudent or brash matches forward, meaning presumptuous in manner.

clue.text: Glugging last drop of amaretto, I bet a man that's sozzled can't stand

indicators.note: sozzled means drunk, so the letters are mixed up
glugging the last drop of a drink means taking only its final letter here

explanation.surface: A drunken bet in a bar over a glass of amaretto.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Glugging' just says the man drinks in the final O of amaretto; 'last drop of' picks that letter and 'sozzled' mixes it with I BET A MAN.
explanation.definitionFit: To abominate is to loathe or detest, which is what it means to be unable to stand something.

clue.text: It's OK to crack brick

definitions.meaning: one fit to break open and eat
a brick is an old-fashioned word for a reliable, decent person

explanation.surface: A builder decides it's fine to crack a brick.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brick' is old British slang for a dependable sort, the same compliment as a good egg.
explanation.definitionFit: Both a brick and a good egg are dated praise for a kind, trustworthy person.

clue.text: Funny dog is out endlessly barking

parts.note: a cur is a mongrel dog

indicators.note: barking means mad, so the letters are scrambled
endlessly means the last letter of out is dropped

explanation.surface: A funny dog has gone out, barking without end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' trims OUT to OU, and 'barking' rearranges IS + OU into IOUS.
explanation.definitionFit: Funny in the sense of odd or strange is a synonym of curious.

clue.text: Describing some stones, colour diminished

parts.note: rose is a pink colour
cut means reduced or diminished

explanation.surface: A description of gems whose colour has faded.
explanation.definitionFit: Rose-cut refers to a gemstone style with a flat base and faceted dome, used for some diamonds.

clue.text: Fly round state in subjugation

indicators.note: round means the sly letters go around the stating word

parts.note: fly as an adjective means sly or cunning
to aver is to state firmly

explanation.surface: An insect flies around a country held in subjugation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fly' looks like an insect or verb but is the adjective meaning crafty.
explanation.definitionFit: Slavery is the condition of being subjugated, held in bondage by another.

clue.text: Capital: money stolen by staff

indicators.note: something stolen is taken in, so the money goes inside the staff

parts.note: a cane is a walking staff
the yen is Japanese currency

explanation.surface: Capital, in the sense of cash, pinched by employees.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Capital' and 'money' suggest finance, but Cayenne is the capital of French Guiana.
explanation.definitionFit: Cayenne is the chief city and seat of government of French Guiana.

clue.text: Vale where heroic figure finally slaughtered

indicators.note: slaughtered suggests something torn apart, so the letters are rearranged
finally points to the last letter of figure

explanation.surface: A valley where a hero was finally cut down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vale' reads as valley, but it is Latin for farewell, matching the British goodbye CHEERIO.
explanation.definitionFit: Vale is a Latin farewell, and cheerio is informal British for goodbye.

clue.text: Worse bit of hardware, it's a nightmare to set up

indicators.note: set up says the hidden letters are read backwards
bit of says a portion of the following words supplies the letters

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A complaint that a worse bit of computer kit is a nightmare to configure.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'Worse bit' as the definition; 'bit of' is the signal that letters are taken from within the words, leaving 'Worse' as the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Nastier is a comparative meaning more unpleasant, the same as worse.

clue.text: Launch isn't off: one opening

indicators.note: off means gone bad or wrong, so the letters are reordered

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
a gate is an opening in a fence or wall

explanation.surface: A rocket launch isn't cancelled: one opening remains.
explanation.definitionFit: To instigate is to set something in motion, as one would launch a campaign.

clue.text: Food from 'B' onward?

definitions.meaning: read as two words: everything beyond the alphabet's first letter

explanation.surface: A question of food starting with B, hinting at a menu.
explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer as PAST A: everything from B onward lies beyond A.
explanation.definitionFit: Pasta is Italian food made from durum wheat dough, such as spaghetti.

clue.text: Appear when parent has surfaced?

parts.note: pop is an informal word for father, a parent
something that has surfaced is up

explanation.surface: Turning up when a father has come to the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: To pop up is an idiom for to arrive or appear suddenly.

clue.text: Bat pinched all the spider's legs, reportedly

indicators.note: reportedly means the words are heard rather than written

parts.note: nicked is informal British for pinched, and a spider has eight legs

explanation.surface: A bat snatched up all of a spider's legs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bat' looks like the animal, but to bat an eyelid is to blink.
explanation.definitionFit: To nictate is to blink or wink, as when one bats the eyelids.

clue.text: Snake — or rat?

definitions.meaning: a rat is a despicable person

explanation.surface: Choosing between a snake and a rat.
explanation.definitionFit: A snake belongs to the class of reptiles, and reptile is also slang for a contemptible, sneaky person.

clue.text: Young girl has been rude about boy at the back wearing hat

indicators.note: wearing the hat means sitting inside it, so the rest goes within the hat

parts.note: a topper is a top hat

indicators.note: about means the jumbled letters go around the picked letter
rude here means rough and unrefined, so the letters are jumbled
at the back picks the final letter of boy

explanation.surface: A girl was rude about a boy sitting at the back in a hat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rude' scrambles the fodder to EENB, 'about' wraps it round Y to make EENYB, and 'wearing' puts that inside the hat.
explanation.definitionFit: A teenybopper is a young teenage girl keen on pop music and fashion.
